key_insight: The paper turns unambiguous pure-state discrimination into a lightweight hybrid quantum-classical SDP with only N scalar optimization variables by using reciprocal states and the discriminated states as the ansatz.
engineering_relevance: It offers a NISQ-friendly route to design POVMs from circuit-prepared states, with error-aware bounds that help make quantum measurement pipelines more reliable on noisy hardware.
method: Represent the discrimination problem as an SDP within NSS using quantum-estimated quantities and classical optimization.
Choose the target pure states as the ansatz and exploit the reciprocal-state representation to reduce the SDP to N scalar variables.
Derive robustness bounds and a rescaling step to keep the POVM valid under bounded Gram-matrix estimation error.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the robustness bounds and finite-shot scaling in simulations and further test overlap estimation on IBM quantum hardware before evaluating the resulting POVMs.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate Gram-matrix estimates and the validity of the perturbation bound, so hardware noise and shot counts can still limit practical discrimination quality.
paper_title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
